children: The estimated funding level of pension plans sponsored by S&P 1500 companies increased by 1 percentage point in September to 113% as a result of an increase in discount rates slightly offset by a decrease in equity markets, according to professional-services firm Marsh. As of the end of September, the plans' estimated aggregate surplus increased by $6 billion, to $181 billion, compared with a $175 billion surplus at the end of August, Marsh says. "Pension funded status for the S&P 1500 rose 1% percent in September after interest rates climbed to 17-year highs," said Marsh partner Matt McDaniel. "Persistent inflation and high energy costs kept pressure on rates, prompting the Fed to raise them by a quarter point in September." (jennifer.williams@wsj.com; @jenkayw)
